title: Types, Parsing, Option, and Result
summary: Use immutable bindings, explicit mutability, scalar and compound types, parsing, pattern matching, Option, Result, and error propagation.
learningObjectives: Explain and apply Types, Parsing, Option, and Result
Use compiler, lint, and test evidence to verify behavior
prerequisiteConcepts: Ability to create and save a text file

sections.heading: Core model
sections.content: Bindings are immutable unless declared `mut`. Rust infers many local types but public contracts should remain clear. Tuples and arrays have fixed shape; `String` owns growable UTF-8 text while `&str` is a borrowed string slice. Parsing returns `Result`, so success and failure must be handled. `Option<T>` represents a value that may be absent without using null. Match both variants or use combinators when they remain readable. The `?` operator returns an error to the caller after conversion; it does not ignore failure.
commonMistakes: interior mutability follows separate runtime rules
byte indexing is unavailable because UTF-8 boundaries matter
